correctedState: Confirmed with two added details. The default matches Claude's MCP_TIMEOUT semantics: packages/shared/src/mcp/mcp-pool.ts:205 `MCP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` is the per-server connect deadline, applied in connectWithDeadline (:1196-1198), and :689 makes it overridable only via the programmatic `connectTimeoutMs` option. The single production construction site, defaultCreatePool at packages/server-core/src/mcp/workspace-mcp-pool-registry.ts:789, does not pass that option, so 30 s is fixed in every shipped path; there is no MCP_TIMEOUT and no NESSY_-prefixed reader anywhere in source (contrast NESSY_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT, which IS read at mcp-pool.ts:1959). Added detail 1 — our constant's SPELLING collides with a different Claude env var: Claude's own MCP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS (env-vars.md:406) is the 5000 ms blocking-startup batch wait, explicitly distinct from MCP_TIMEOUT; any fix should not reuse our current name for an env var. Added detail 2 — our budget is tighter than the doc's, not merely unraisable: the 3-attempt initial-connect retry (MCP_CONNECT_RETRY, workspace-mcp-pool-registry.ts) runs INSIDE the single 30 s deadline (mcp-pool.ts:655-661, connectWithDeadline races connectWithRetries against it), whereas Claude's MCP_TIMEOUT 'bounds an individual server's connect attempt'. So the exact scenario the doc describes — a first run slow while npx downloads the package — is bounded by 30 s shared across all retries, with no operator lever to raise it. Also: per-server `timeout` in .mcp.json is routed to toolTimeoutMs (project-config.ts:98-99), i.e. tool execution, and the per-server `timeout` at mcp/validation.ts:317 belongs to the config test-connection path, not the runtime pool — neither is an override for this deadline.
